newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar idles in Singapore ahead of Buba repo, Fed.
newsitem.headline: Dollar idles in Singapore ahead of Buba repo, Fed.

text.p: The U.S. dollar sat on its hands on Tuesday as Singapore players awaited the Bundesbank's decision on money market rates and the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later in the day.
"There's very little going on with the Buba repo and FOMC later on. No one's doing anything ahead of that," a European bank dealer said.
Dealers said the market was not expecting a rate change from either the German or the U.S. central banks but participants were reluctant to take up fresh positions until they were sure.

Speculation the Bundesbank would raise interest rates was dampened after Buba council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday a rise in German interest rates right now would be damaging to the economy.
"I'd think there's a possibility of the dollar going higher on the back of nothing happening with the repo and everyone will probably sell into that," the dealer said.
He said the 1.8380 marks level was going to pose a good technical barrier for the dollar while 118.30 yen was also proving to be a tough resistance.

But he added that the dollar remained on an overall uptrend. "After we've had no moves by both (central banks), that's kind of a reaffirmation of the interest rate differential. So people are likely to go back to selling marks," he said.

San Paolo Bank in Singapore said in a daily research bulletin that even if a German repo rate hike became necessary to maintain the Bundesbank's credibility and strengthen the mark in the coming weeks, it was unlikely to be followed by a rise in official interest rates.
